Incident practice notes.

Workarounds applied during an incident are temporary by construction. Recording
one without an expiry produces a rule that outlives the condition it addressed.
The convention is to record the workaround with an explicit validity interval and
to let it expire rather than to remember to remove it.

A revert is evidence. A proposal that was raised and rejected tells you something
the absence of a proposal does not: that the alternative was considered and
declined. Discarding rejected proposals loses that information and invites the
same proposal again.

Repetition is not corroboration. Ten restatements of one prior are one piece of
evidence repeated, and counting them as ten independent supports will move a
decision that a single independent observation should not have moved.
